column3: The Hebrew repeats the inheriting root in receiving and assigning the inheritance and names the sons of Israel twice; BSB uses “inherited” and “distributed” and ends with “Israel.”
The Hebrew says “by the hand of Moses”; BSB says “through Moses.”
The Hebrew says “beyond the Jordan” without an explicit word “east”; BSB specifies “east of the Jordan.”
The Hebrew actively says “they did not give” a portion and distinguishes livestock and property; BSB uses “no portion ... was given” and “flocks and herds.”
The Hebrew describes the report as “according to what was with my heart”; BSB calls it “an honest report.”
The Hebrew uses singular “the heart of the people” and says Caleb “filled after” the LORD; BSB has plural “hearts,” supplies “with fear,” and says “remained loyal.”
The Hebrew says “your sons”; BSB uses the broader “your children”.
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD twice and repeats “now, behold”; BSB uses “He” for the second name and varies the second introduction as “So here I am.”
The Hebrew repeats “on that day” and says “perhaps the LORD is with me”; BSB has “then” and “Perhaps with the LORD’s help.”
The Hebrew says Joshua blessed “him” and then names Caleb as the recipient of Hebron; BSB names Caleb with the blessing and uses “him” for the gift.
The Hebrew gives the former name Kiriath-arba and then says “he was the great man among the Anakim”; BSB makes the connection explicit with “after Arba.”
